summary: Redwood conducted a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for inference and is interested in per-route cost allocation, token-level analytics, sampling to validate model regressions, and security/KMS concerns. Agreed next steps: send pricing and cost spreadsheet, share security docs, schedule 2-week pilot and dedicated-demo follow-up.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE. Priya is our solutions engineer. Uh, Carlos, Sara, Tom, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Carlos (OmniFlow CTO): Thanks Jordan. We got a short agenda, want to see the console, the usage analytics, and especially per-route cost - that's been a pain for us.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Great - today we'll jump into the Console, show the per-route dashboards, how cost is broken down to token level, and how you can slice traffic and do sampling for quality checks.
[00:32] Tom (Eng): Quick context - we run a mix of generation and embeddings, about 6 million tokens/day currently, mostly for chat features. Key constraints: predictable cost, low p50 latency for 95th percentile use, and data residency for EU customers.
[00:48] Sara (Infra): Also interested in dedicated capacity if that helps with latency predictability and audit logs.
[00:55] Priya: Noted. We'll show hosted defaults then point out dedicated behavior. Jumping in - Console home, usage overview. You can see total tokens, requests, avg latency, and cost over time.
[01:10] Jordan: One handy thing is the cost waterfall - infra, model unit, caching savings. We surface estimated per-token unit economics alongside raw invoices so you're not guessing.
[01:23] Carlos: Can you show per-route? We have several routes: /chat, /summarize, /embeddings-batch, and they vary by prompt length.
[01:31] Priya: Yep - here's the routes table. Each route has its own QPS, token distribution histogram, and cost per 1M tokens. Note the per-route breakdown ties back to your tagging - so microservices or teams can be billed correctly.
[01:50] Tom: How is the cost computed? OpenAI style or your own units?
[01:54] Priya: We compute based on model profile (tokens per second, expected cost for model variant) plus infra amortization. For hosted it's our visible unit price; for Dedicated we show an effective per-token cost based on your reserved capacity plus utilization.
[02:10] Sara: So for Dedicated, if we underutilize, the per-token cost goes up?
[02:13] Priya: Exactly. The console shows projected cost curves by utilization, and we provide recommendations - e.g., increase batching or use a quantized variant during off-peak to improve unit economics.
[02:25] Jordan: Also worth calling out automatic caching - prefix/KV cache reductions are shown as a separate line in the waterfall.
[02:33] Carlos: Is KV cache visible per-route?
[02:36] Priya: Yes - cache hit rate per route, and you can drill into top keys, TTLs, and estimated savings. Sometimes our transcripts show 'K-V cash' in exports, heh.
[02:47] (laughter)
[02:50] Jordan: Moving to the per-token drilldown - here's a heatmap of token length distribution by route, and below that is token-cost attribution. You can filter by model version to see how a newer model affects cost and latency.
[03:08] Tom: Can you show an example where a new model increased latency but reduced token count? We saw that with another vendor.
[03:13] Priya: Sure. Flip to this demo trace: route /summarize, model v1.4 -> v1.5. v1.5 reduced avg output tokens by 18% but adds 30ms per-token compute; overall cost decreased because token reduction outweighed latency cost for throughput-bound workloads.
[03:32] Carlos: Nice, we need those tradeoff charts.
[03:35] Priya: We also have per-route SLO overlays; you can set p95 latency targets and the console highlights when a route is violating. Then you can configure fallback policies - e.g., if hosted model is slow, route to a cheaper quantized variant or to dedicated pool.
[03:52] Sara: About routing - can we route by region and customer tier? We need EU traffic to stay in eu-west.
[03:58] Jordan: Yes, smart routing exists - region, cost, latency, and you can pin by customer tier. For Private deployments we do enforced residency via VPC/on-prem deployments.
[04:12] Tom: Security nit - how do you handle keys? We need KMS/HSM integration and per-request encryption.
[04:18] Priya: We integrate with customer KMS for key management, and logs are truncated for PII; you can configure full audit logs for Dedicated/Private. We'll attach security docs.
[04:28] Carlos: SOC 2?
[04:30] Jordan: Yes, SOC 2 Type II; we have ISO plans as well. We'll share the pack.
[04:36] Priya: Back to analytics - sampling and quality monitoring. You can configure sampling rules by route: e.g., capture 1% of chat traffic and auto-run evals on prompt sets to detect regressions. Alerts tie to prompt-based tests.
[04:52] Tom: Is sampling done pre or post-aggregation? We want to avoid PII in samples.
[04:57] Priya: Sampling can be applied at proxy level before persistence; you can opt for anonymization and redaction.
[05:05] Carlos: For cost allocation, do you support tags and billing exports?
[05:09] Jordan: Yes, tags map to cost centers in the billing export. You can download per-route CSVs or push to your billing pipeline.
[05:18] Sara: Any best practices to reduce cost without losing quality?
[05:21] Priya: Common ones: prefix caching, dynamic batching, model distillation/quantized variants for non-critical routes, and smart sampling to prioritize evals. We also show recommended batching windows per route - you can set server-side batching policies.
[05:37] Tom: How do you measure batching impact on latency?
[05:40] Priya: The console simulates latency curves based on batch size vs p50/p95; you can also run a synthetic benchmark from the UI to validate.
[05:48] Jordan: Quick demo of a per-route anomaly: here's a spike in token usage on /chat from a bot misconfiguration. We drill into the trace and set an alert rule to auto-scale or throttle.
[06:03] Carlos: That helps. For the pilot, we want to run a 2-week litmus using a copy of our staging traffic on a dedicated pool to see real numbers.
[06:12] Jordan: Good plan - we'll propose a window and a traffic slice. Priya will outline the benchmarking steps.
[06:19] Priya: Steps: (1) create a dedicated pool or a hosted experiment with pinned capacity, (2) run your staging replay for X hours/day for two weeks, (3) we collect per-route cost and quality metrics and provide a final report.
[06:33] Sara: Is there a cost for the pilot?
[06:36] Jordan: Usually we offer pilot credits, but depends on scale; we'll include pricing options in the sheet.
[06:42] Tom: Competitors question - how is this better than running in-house on SageMaker?
[06:46] Priya: Redwood focuses on inference ops: optimized runtimes, kernel selection, continuous batching, and built-in observability. Running in-house requires the same tooling and ops overhead; we give a unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private.
[07:02] Carlos: What's the SLA for Dedicated?
[07:05] Jordan: SLA depends on contract tier; standard dedicated SLAs cover uptime and latency targets. We'll include that in the follow-up.
[07:12] (longer demo interlude: Priya clicks through dashboards, shows CSV export, config UI)
[20:05] Priya: Showing the per-route cost spreadsheet export now - it includes tokens, requests, model variant, estimated compute cost, infra amortization, and cache savings. You can import into your own chargeback system.
[20:25] Tom: The CSV sample looks good. Can you make the model-version column machine-friendly? Sometimes product names get munged.
[20:31] Priya: Yep, we use canonical model ids and human-friendly names.
[20:35] Carlos: Any gotchas?
[20:38] Jordan: Watch out for tail latency on long context prompts; for those you may want larger GPU instances or pinned dedicated routes. Also, underutilization of Dedicated increases unit cost - the console will flag that.
[20:51] Sara: Ok, security doc and KMS integration will be the gating item for us.
[20:56] Jordan: Understood. We'll send the SOC2 + KMS integration notes.
[21:02] Priya: Final recap: we'll send pricing & per-route spreadsheet, security pack, and a pilot proposal. Recommend follow-up dedicated-demo after pilot planning.
[21:12] Carlos: Sounds good. Thanks Jordan, Priya.
[21:15] Tom: Thanks.
[21:16] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the notes and action items.
[21:20] (call ends, ~46 minutes)
